trickyParts: The claim's activity columns are deliberately absent from `putClaim`'s `on conflict do update`, so a machine's claim write cannot erase a session's report. Anything deciding on them must read the store, never a live `Machine.Claim()`, which shows the zero values until the claim is reloaded.

A release is three acts on the issue's lifecycle lane in order: the save (`issue_bundle`), the role stops (`supervise` op `release`), the teardown (`issue_release`). The save must precede the stops because only the role's shim can run jj in the workspace. R4's boundary is the first role stop, so the save sits before it and a wake arriving during the save cancels the release and its bundle.

`ByRule()` names only the sources the boot resumes (`daemon`, `exit`); a released claim is resumed by the wake, not the boot, and `RuleMayResume()` (negative on `operator` alone) is what makes `deliverResuming` and `resumeByRule` work for it unchanged.

The daemon addresses the claims and pod tables by the project token and the Dispatch mirror by the project key. `workflow.Config` now carries both; mixing them is invisible at compile time and was one of the three defects this round found.

The acceptance rig runs one role per pod and starts the launcher in its single-role form, because the roles-dir form makes Linux user, mount, PID and IPC namespaces over the worker image's layout, which this container has not. The daemon's side of the protocol is identical, but the rig therefore does not exercise role namespaces or the once-per-pod restore, which `internal/runtime/sandbox`'s own test covers instead.

discoveredComplexity: Three defects fatal to the whole feature were found only by the acceptance rig, each invisible to every unit test because each half of the seam was tested alone. (1) The listener built its wake report's envelope without `source_event_id`, which `contracts.Envelope.Validate` requires, so every report including `listener_ready` was dropped before publication and no pod could ever be released. (2) The workflow engine addressed the pod tables by the project key while the daemon addressed them by the token, so engine writes and daemon reads never met. (3) The release stopped every role process before the teardown asked one of those roles' shims for the bundle, so every release was cancelled with `bundle_save_failed`. Each is fixed here with a regression test that drives both sides of its seam.

A fourth gap: nothing on the daemon side read a saved bundle back or sent it to the replacement pod's launcher, so R2's restore half was unwired — both ends existed and were unit-tested, and `grep` for `SplitWorkspaceBundle` outside tests found only its own declaration. The runtime now sends the slices before any `launcher_start` and deletes the stored bundle on the launcher's `Held`.

`workflowRuntime.idleTick`'s comment says a test shortens it, but nothing sets it and nothing reachable from the daemon's boot can, so the rig waits out the real one-minute tick. Not changed here; it is why the rig costs 217 s rather than 30.

A direct message to a session that also holds an interest in its own agent subject may be delivered twice: the listener's subscribe handler appends the agent subject to a session's stored topics, so the session is reachable on both the interest fan-out and the agent-subject path. Seen once while building the rig, not chased, and nothing was changed for it; it is `packages/envoy`'s to judge.
